conceptBreakdown.content:
Enzymes are biological catalysts (Biocatalysts) that speed up biochemical reactions by orders of magnitude without undergoing permanent chemical changes.

### General Properties & Ribozyme Exception
• **Proteinaceous Nature**: Most enzymes are globular proteins possessing tertiary and quaternary structures with specific **Active Sites**.
• **Ribozymes (Non-Protein Catalysts)**: Specific RNA molecules with enzymatic properties (*e.g., 23S rRNA peptidyl transferase in prokaryotic ribosomes, RNase P, self-splicing group I/II introns*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Thermodynamic Principles of Catalysis
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Thermodynamic Principles of Catalysis
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Lowering Activation Energy ($\Delta G^\ddagger$)**: Enzymes stabilize the high-energy, unstable **Transition State ($S^\ddagger$)** by providing alternative reaction pathways with lower activation energy barriers.
• **Thermodynamic Invariance**:
  1. Enzymes do **NOT alter the standard free energy change ($\Delta G$)** of the reaction.
  2. Enzymes do **NOT alter the equilibrium constant ($K_{\text{eq}}$)** or the final concentrations of reactants and products.
  3. Enzymes merely accelerate the speed at which chemical equilibrium is reached.
